checks.label: Plot the points and create a right triangle much as for the slope: on every screen the run arrow goes straight across from the first point, the rise arrow straight up or down to the second, and a right-angle mark sits where they meet

Derived from the Pythagorean theorem, the distance formula finds the distance between two points: every distance row ends in the square root of the run squared plus the rise squared, the long side is labelled the same, and each distance puzzle accepts only that answer

To find the midpoint, find the average of the x-axis coordinates and the average of the y-axis coordinates: every midpoint row ends in that pair, the marker sits there, its dashed lines meet the number scales at the two averages, and each midpoint puzzle accepts only that answer

Every worked row is right, by hand: √100 = 10 four times, √25 = 5, √169 = 13 twice, √73 ≈ 8.5 for B dragged to (4, 10), midpoints (4, 6), (5, 5), (1, 2), (−1, 2), (7, 4.5) and (2.5, 6), and B at (7, 10) and (7, −2) by working back

A negative difference leaves its square, and so the distance, unchanged: with A at (1, 2), B at (7, 10), (7, −6) and (−5, −6) all give 36 + 64 = 100 and d = 10, and starting from B gives the same distance as starting from A
The distance is never shorter than the larger difference nor longer than the two added: 8 ≤ 10 ≤ 14 for (−2, 7) and (4, −1), and the same on every distance screen

The midpoint lands on the long side, the same distance from each end, and its dashed lines cross the run and the rise at their halfway points and reach the number scales, wherever B is dragged on the first midpoint screen
Working back takes the same step again: on both working-back screens the step from M to B equals the step from A to M, so M is the midpoint of A and B, and B is never the midpoint of A and M
Before an answer a puzzle draws no triangle and no marker, and its working reads ?; a right answer or Why? draws them and fills in the working; every wrong answer has a hint of its own

Every wrong answer offered is a real slip worked from the puzzle's own points: run plus rise, no square root, dropped brackets, halved differences, totals not halved, a lost minus, the midpoint of A and M, or the step alone
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; a puzzle's drawing finishes within 2.5 s
